cases.description: At least the declared number of passes is performed: a chain that settles in exactly that many passes settles, with nothing to report.
On reaching the pass limit the last settled text is returned with its placeholder unresolved, nothing raises, and pass-limit is reported once with origin limit.
At least the declared number of characters of output is permitted: an output of exactly that length is produced whole, with nothing to report.
A pass whose output would exceed the limit is discarded whole, so the message as it reached the first pass is what settles, and output-limit is reported once with origin limit.
A placeholder past the output limit is neither resolved nor reported, and the host-defined modifier it names is not called.
A serialization that reaches the conversion limit is a conversion that cannot describe the value: the placeholder takes the chain and unserializable-value is reported with origin payload.

A limit ends the process the way a settling pass does, so the single removal of escape sequences still runs over the text the pass limit stopped, which a self-referential value reaches whatever the limit is.
